Shifted schedule (Sunday-Thursday)

About Conception:

Conception is pioneering the future of reproductive biology by generating functional human eggs from induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). Our mission is to unlock new possibilities for fertility, reproductive health, and genetic diversity. We are building a world-class team to make this vision a reality.

The role:

We are looking for an experienced stem cell scientist who genuinely enjoys maintaining and handling human pluripotent stem cells and wants to build a career doing this work extremely well.
This person should take real ownership of culture quality. You should have strong judgment around what healthy cultures look like, notice when something is starting to go wrong, and have a “do no harm” mindset around handling sensitive cells and minimizing unnecessary stress.
A big part of the job is also the discipline that comes with good cell culture: careful documentation, tracking culture history, maintaining cell banks, following QC closely, and working to reduce batch-to-batch variability as much as possible. We want someone who enjoys this part of the work too and takes pride in being meticulous.
This is a very hands-on role. We are specifically looking for someone who likes being at the hood, likes caring for cells, and wants to become exceptionally good at it.

Availability for the Sunday–Thursday schedule is critical to our workflows, and we offer a salary adjustment for this schedule.

What you’ll do:

Maintain human iPSC/ESC cultures: Culture, passage, expand, freeze and thaw sensitive stem cell lines while maintaining consistently high culture quality.
Own culture quality: Develop strong judgment around morphology, confluency, differentiation, recovery and overall culture health, and identify problems early.
Minimize culture stress: Handle cells carefully and consistently, paying attention to small differences in technique that can affect quality and downstream performance.
Reduce variability: Help make our stem cell workflows as consistent and reproducible as possible across operators and batches.
Support cell banks and QC: Maintain cell banks and perform routine QC, including mycoplasma and sterility testing, characterization and sample preparation for whole-genome sequencing.
Perform directed differentiations: Run routine differentiations with careful attention to timing, handling and outcome tracking.
Improve processes: Help stabilize protocols, define QC standards and ultimately contribute to process development for our stem cell workflows.
Document everything well: Maintain clear, accurate culture records, track deviations and outcomes, and help ensure that culture history is easy to understand and trace.
Prepare critical reagents: Prepare media, small molecules and other cell culture reagents consistently and carefully.

Experience:

Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in biology, stem cell biology, or a related field
Hands-on experience maintaining human iPSC and/or ESC cultures
Industry experience strongly preferred
Strong sterile technique and excellent judgment around healthy versus poor-quality stem cell cultures
Strong attention to detail, documentation, and record-keeping
Experience working to improve consistency and reduce batch-to-batch variability
Prior hands-on flow cytometry experience
Comfortable with repetitive, detail-oriented work where consistency really matters
Someone who genuinely enjoys tissue culture and wants this to be a meaningful part of their long-term career
Positive attitude and strong team mindset

We are open to candidates across the Senior Research Associate / Associate Scientist range, including PhD-level candidates. Level and title will be based on relevant experience, technical depth, and demonstrated independence.

Why join us:

Impact: Be part of a high-reliability stem cell core that underpins our preclinical pipeline, with the potential to transform human reproduction
Growth: Gain experience with cutting-edge stem cell culture methods and QC approaches
Community: Work alongside passionate scientists tackling one of the most exciting frontiers in biology with a deeply aligned team
Mission: Build the biological foundation for a new era of reproductive medicine, expanding what is possible for millions of people and families with limited options today

Position Summary

The Research Associate, Analytical Sciences will be responsible for the execution of routine testing, including but not limited to molecular biology assays and cell-based assays and to characterize T cell therapy processes and products. Additionally, this role contributes to the daily operational tasks in the Analytical Sciences team. This role is based in Santa Monica, CA.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

Perform routine analytical testing to characterize cell products or processes primarily using DNA/RNA extraction/quantification, dPCR, live cell imaging, and plate-based assays.
Accurately complete eLN documentation contemporaneously for the lab work in which it pertains to.
Participate in eLN template drafting, revisions, and ensure executable templates are comprehensive.
Participate in tracking assay results and test method performance parameters.
Assist in everyday operation of analytical laboratories, including but not limited to equipment management, lab maintenance and restocking, and reagent inventory.
Support cross-functional projects with process development, manufacturing, quality control, and quality assurance groups.

Responsibilities

What the Role Entails (Day-to-Day Responsibilities)

Sample Processing & Genomics:
Daily processing of samples using genomic workflows (DNA extractions, running PCR / dPCR).
Culturing, handling, and preparing human T cells / mammalian cells.

Lab Operations & Inventory:
Managing reagent inventory and placing orders for consumables as they are used.
Reporting instrument issues/faults to ensure quick maintenance and calibration.

Data Analysis & Documentation:
Performing basic data analysis and maintaining standard lab records/documentation.

Hands-on experience in performing and analyzing qPCR/dPCR and/or cell-based assays is preferred.

Department Information

Vision

We enhance public safety and promote successful community reintegration through education, treatment and active participation in rehabilitative and restorative justice programs.

Mission

To facilitate the successful reintegration of the individuals in our care back to their communities equipped with the tools to be drug-free, healthy, and employable members of society by providing education, treatment, rehabilitative, and restorative justice programs, all in a safe and humane environment.

CDCR and CCHCS are committed to transforming the correctional landscape to create safer, more professional, and more fulfilling environments for our employees, the incarcerated population, and those supervised in our communities. Through systemwide improvements grounded in proven and emerging practices, we aim to strengthen rehabilitation, enhance workplace satisfaction, and support successful reentry into the community through our institutions, parole, and community partnerships. Our shared mission is to promote safety, wellness, and human dignity while fostering positive change for all those who live and work within our institutions and communities

CDCR and CCHCS are committed to building an inclusive respectful workplace. We are determined to attract and hire candidates from all communities and empower employees from a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and personal experiences. We are proud to foster inclusion and drive collaborative efforts at all levels of the Department.

Across our organization, our programs work cooperatively to provide the highest level of health care possible to a diverse correctional population. We encourage creativity and ingenuity while treating others fairly, honestly, and with respect, all of which are critical to the success of the CDCR and CCHCS mission.

This advertisement is for a Senior Laboratory Assistant, Correctional Facility position(s) located at Centinela State Prison (CEN) in Imperial, in Imperial County. Please indicate the position number on your application: 403-000-9266-XXX.

Note:
Main communication for this position will be through email. Please ensure you have a valid email address on your application.

Department Website: https://cchcs.ca.gov/careers

Effective July 1, 2025, in accordance with the applicable Memorandum of Understanding, the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025) was implemented in response to the status of the State budget. Salaries do not reflect the recent changes. Part-time employees are subject to the same conditions as full-time employees, on a prorated basis equivalent to their time-base. Permanent intermittent employees are subject to the same condition as full-time employees, based on the number of hours worked in the pay period.

May act in a lead capacity for laboratory assistants. Maintains order and supervises the conduct of the incarcerated and protects and maintains the safety of persons and property.
